science.title: Strength needs water too
science.text: Creatine is the most-researched supplement for strength and power — it helps your muscles regenerate energy for those last hard reps. But creatine also pulls water into your muscle cells, so hydration matters more. We pair a full 5 g dose with sodium, potassium and magnesium, so you build strength and stay hydrated at the same time.

format.title: Creatine that hydrates
format.text: Most creatine is flavourless powder you choke down in water. This one mixes into a light, lightly sweet electrolyte drink — easy to sip before or during training.

steps.title: One scoop in water
steps.text: Mix 1 scoop (10 g) into 10–16 oz of water and stir or shake until dissolved.

steps.title: Before or during training
steps.text: Sip it before or during your workout for hydration, or any time to top up your daily creatine.

steps.title: Every day
steps.text: Creatine works best taken daily and consistently — even on rest days — to keep your muscles saturated.

items.a: Creatine draws water into your muscles, so staying hydrated matters even more. Adding sodium, potassium and magnesium replaces what you sweat out — so you get strength and proper hydration in one scoop.

items.q: Do I need to load creatine?
items.a: No loading phase needed — take one 5 g scoop daily and your muscles will saturate over a couple of weeks. Just be consistent.
Any time works, but before or during training gives you hydration when you need it. Take it daily, including rest days.
Creatine can cause a little water retention in the muscle early on — that's normal and settles. The electrolytes actually help your fluid balance.
If you're pregnant or nursing, under 18, have kidney issues, or follow a sodium-restricted diet, consult a physician before use.
